clue.text: Attack from a small boat

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
sail can mean a ship or boat, as in a fleet of fifty sail

explanation.surface: Pirates or raiders launch an assault from a little dinghy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link word joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail someone is to launch a violent assault on them.

clue.text: Teasing whilst knitting the welt

explanation.surface: Someone gets mocked while busy with their needles on a sweater's edge.
explanation.walkthrough: The welt is the stretchy band at a jumper's (sweater's) cuff or hem, usually worked in alternating plain and purl stitches.
explanation.definitionFit: Good-natured mockery is a form of banter, and the ridged knit-and-purl pattern at a garment's edge carries the same name.

clue.text: Promote retiring Italian in hostile environment

indicators.note: an environment surrounds something, so the hostile word encloses the Italian piece

parts.note: adverse means hostile or unfavourable

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the letters for Italian are read backwards

parts.note: IT is a standard abbreviation for Italian, as in Italian vermouth

explanation.surface: Publicise a shy Italian who finds himself in unfriendly surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' pretends to mean shy, but it reads the abbreviation backwards; 'environment' means the hostile word surrounds it.
explanation.definitionFit: To promote a product is to publicise it in order to sell it.

clue.text: Disregard some design or embellishment

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Pay no attention to part of a pattern or a piece of decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across desIGN OR Embellishment.
explanation.definitionFit: To disregard something is to pay it no attention or overlook it.

clue.text: Naval NCO produced hair-oil

parts.note: PO is a petty officer, a non-commissioned officer in the navy
made is a synonym of produced

explanation.surface: A petty officer in the navy has manufactured a grooming product for slicking hair.
explanation.walkthrough: PO (petty officer) is a crossword staple for a naval NCO.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomade is a scented ointment used to dress and slick the hair.

clue.text: Stewed pears man served with cheese

indicators.note: stewed fruit is cooked down into a mush, so the letters of pears man are mixed up

explanation.surface: A dessert of cooked pears is served alongside cheese by a waiter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served with' is a link word; 'Stewed' rearranges PEARS MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Parmesan is a hard Italian cheese, often grated over pasta.

clue.text: Montana houses solitary French artist

indicators.note: houses means holds within, so the state's abbreviation encloses the word for solitary

parts.note: MT is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Montana
solitary means single, alone, one

explanation.surface: A lonely French painter lives somewhere in Montana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' pretends to mean dwellings in the state, but signals that the state's abbreviation holds the word for solitary.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Monet was the French Impressionist painter of the water lilies.

clue.text: Pay no attention to deduction

explanation.surface: Ignore the reduction in price being offered.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is a verb, the other a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss an idea is to set it aside, and a reduction taken off a price is also called this.

clue.text: Parties must be quiet in lodgings

parts.note: SH is the hush someone says to demand quiet
digs is British slang for rented lodgings

explanation.surface: No noise is allowed at parties held in rented rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be' is a link word. DIGS is British slang for a rented room, especially a student's.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is a lively party or celebration.

clue.text: Awful cronies covered with hair

indicators.note: awful means dreadful or messed up, so the letters of cronies are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ghastly old pals are covered in hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' rearranges CRONIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Crinose is a rare word meaning hairy, from Latin crinis, a hair.

clue.text: Fit enough to encompass mile walk

indicators.note: to encompass means to surround, so the word for fit enough goes around the mile

parts.note: able means fit enough or capable

explanation.surface: Someone is fit enough to manage a walk of a mile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to encompass' puts M inside ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to stroll at a leisurely pace.

clue.text: Welcome to the wedding breakfast

explanation.surface: A greeting extended at the meal after a marriage ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the' is a link word. A wedding breakfast is the British term for the meal after a wedding, whatever the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: A greeting given to guests is one sense, and the party held after a marriage ceremony is the other.

clue.text: Aim to wind up

explanation.surface: Plan to finish things off.
explanation.definitionFit: A goal or purpose is one sense, and to finish or conclude is the other.

clue.text: Let down many an engineer afterwards

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a crossword sense of many
then means afterwards or next

explanation.surface: An engineer is disappointed later on, like many before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an' is a link word. Let down is meant in the dressmaker's sense of letting down a hem.
explanation.definitionFit: Letting down a hem or trouser leg makes the garment longer.

clue.text: Company about which prince Edward was passionate

explanation.surface: A royal was enthusiastic about his own production business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was' is a link word. Prince Edward founded a TV production company, Ardent Productions, in 1993.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the prince's television firm is also an adjective for eager and fervent.

clue.text: Hound socialist compiler

parts.note: red is a common label for a socialist or communist
a setter is the person who compiles a crossword

explanation.surface: Hunting down a left-wing puzzle maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hound' looks like a verb but is the noun: a breed of dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish setter, with its chestnut coat, is a gundog breed.

clue.text: In a religious house it takes precedence

indicators.note: takes means holds inside, so the religious house encloses the word it

parts.note: a priory is a monastery or convent run by a prior or prioress

explanation.surface: Inside a monastery, something comes first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link word; 'takes' signals that the religious house holds the word it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with first claim on attention has precedence over the rest.

clue.text: Agent makes money in the Seychelles

indicators.note: in places the coin inside the country's code

parts.note: SY is the international vehicle registration code for the Seychelles
P stands for penny or pence, a small coin

explanation.surface: A secret operative earns cash in an island nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' is a link word. SY is the Seychelles' code on car plates.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret agent is someone who gathers intelligence covertly.

clue.text: Pop out more often? No problem!

parts.note: pa and pop are both familiar names for a father
someone who is out more often is, put the other way, in less

explanation.surface: Is Dad going out more? Fine by me!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' is Dad, not a burst; being 'out more often' is turned round into being IN LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something effortless and free of hurt causes no trouble at all.

clue.text: Individual who finished first, they say

indicators.note: they say means the word is spoken, so its sound gives a differently spelt word

parts.note: someone who finished first in a race won it

explanation.surface: The single person who came out on top, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: WON (finished first) sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A single individual is a solitary unit, one person.

clue.text: Unlawful acts by a Ukrainian republic

parts.note: crime is lawbreaking in general

explanation.surface: Illegal deeds committed by a region of Ukraine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link word. The peninsula was an autonomous republic within Ukraine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Black Sea peninsula had the status of an autonomous republic of Ukraine.

clue.text: Spring to fight endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the last letter of the word for fight is removed

parts.note: to spar is to box or fight

explanation.surface: Leap into an unending battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word; 'endlessly' drops the R from SPAR. 'Spring' is the water source, not a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: A mineral spring whose waters are thought healthful is the original sense.

clue.text: Dick gets no work during mini-series

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so the short series surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: SER is a short form of series, so a mini series
taken as written
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A man lands no acting job in a short TV drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is a link word; 'during' signals the shortened series going round the rest. Dick is old slang for a detective.
explanation.definitionFit: A private eye is a professional prier into others' affairs.

clue.text: Intimate chum embraces cockney woman's lad

indicators.note: embraces means hugs, so the word for chum surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: pal means chum or friend
a cockney drops the h, so her becomes 'er
a son is a lad or boy

explanation.surface: A close friend is hugging a London woman's boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraces' signals the friend going round the rest. Cockney is the dialect of working-class East London, known for dropping the h.
explanation.definitionFit: Private or intimate matters are those concerning oneself.

clue.text: Team appearing one by one

explanation.surface: Players coming out in single file.
explanation.walkthrough: The number written in figures is a 1 standing beside another 1.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket side has this many players, and the number is written as two ones side by side.

clue.text: The French entrance an envoy

parts.note: le is the masculine form of the in French
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: A French doorway and a diplomat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A papal representative or ambassador sent on a mission is a legate.

clue.text: Canoeing manoeuvres trainee finds agreeable

indicators.note: manoeuvres means moves around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is for learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A novice paddler finds boat drills pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finds' is a link word; 'manoeuvres' looks like boating drills but signals rearranging the boat word, with the learner's letter tacked on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasant, friendly person or place is agreeable.

clue.text: Add gloss to a Rita hayworth film

parts.note: to gild is to coat with gold or add a showy gloss

explanation.surface: Polishing up a Hollywood classic.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1946 film noir starred Rita Hayworth in the title role.
explanation.definitionFit: Hayworth's best-known film is named after the femme fatale she played.

clue.text: Get piece of leather, albeit no good

parts.note: tho is a short spelling of though, meaning albeit

explanation.surface: Buy a leather strip, even though it is useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a narrow strip of leather used as a lace or strap.

clue.text: Nannies' mates want Aussie cooking-pots

explanation.surface: Childminders' partners need Australian camping kettles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'want' is a link word. 'Nannies' are female goats, not childminders.
explanation.definitionFit: Male goats pair with nanny goats, and Australian bushmen boil tea in tin cans with wire handles of the same name.

clue.text: Tear around perpetually, yet be respectful

indicators.note: around means enclosing, so the word for tear goes about the word for perpetually

parts.note: a rent is a tear or rip
ever means always or perpetually

explanation.surface: Rush about constantly, yet stay polite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yet be' is a link phrase; 'around' signals the tear going round the word for always. 'Tear' pretends to be a verb meaning rush.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing deep respect or awe, as in worship, is to be reverent.

clue.text: Indirect way to enter a conference?

explanation.surface: A detour, or how delegates get in.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word: delegates enter a conference by pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A road skirting a town is an indirect route, and getting into a conference requires showing a badge, so in by pass.
